learningObjectives.title: Five kinds of formula and how to interconvert them
The functional groups and the classes they define
Why boiling points rise along a series
Structural isomers, and primary, secondary, tertiary

questions.q: The diagram shows the skeletal formula of a hydrocarbon. Which condensed structural formula represents the same compound?
optionWhy: You counted the six line segments as six carbon atoms. The lines are bonds; the carbon atoms sit at the line ends and vertices, so the main chain has six carbons, not five, and the branch adds a seventh.

You gave the second carbon two H atoms as if it were an ordinary chain carbon. It is bonded to three carbon atoms, so it can carry only one H atom; written as CH₂ with a CH₃ attached it would have five bonds.

You counted every line end and vertex as a carbon atom: six in the main chain and one at the end of the branch on the second carbon. That carbon is bonded to three carbon atoms, so it is CH; the rest are CH₃ at the ends and CH₂ in the chain. The compound is 2-methylhexane, C₇H₁₆.
You ignored the short vertical line. Its end is a carbon atom too, so it is a CH₃ branch on the second carbon, and that carbon is CH, not CH₂. The compound has seven carbon atoms, not six.
questions.explain: You counted every line end and vertex as a carbon atom: six in the main chain and one at the end of the branch on the second carbon. That carbon is bonded to three carbon atoms, so it is CH; the rest are CH₃ at the ends and CH₂ in the chain. The compound is 2-methylhexane, C₇H₁₆.

questions.q: The diagram shows the skeletal formula of a compound. Which statement about its functional groups is correct?
options: It contains an amido group, since –NH₂ is bonded to a carbon atom.
It contains an ester group, since the C=O carbon is bonded to two carbons.
It is unsaturated, since an –NH₂ group has replaced a hydrogen atom.
It contains amino and ketone groups, since –NH₂ and C=O are on different carbons.
optionWhy: An amido group is –CONH₂, with the nitrogen bonded directly to the carbonyl carbon. Here the NH₂ is on a CH₂ carbon two bonds away from the C=O, so it is an amino group.
An ester group is –COO–, with the carbonyl carbon bonded to a second oxygen atom. A C=O carbon bonded to two carbon atoms is a ketone carbonyl group.
Saturated and unsaturated refer to carbon–carbon bonds. All the carbon–carbon bonds here are single, so the compound is saturated whatever functional groups it carries.

The –NH₂ group bonded to a carbon of the chain is an amino group. The C=O carbon is bonded to two carbon atoms, so it is a ketone carbonyl group. The two groups are on different carbon atoms, so there is no amide.
questions.explain: The –NH₂ group bonded to a carbon of the chain is an amino group. The C=O carbon is bonded to two carbon atoms, so it is a ketone carbonyl group. The two groups are on different carbon atoms, so there is no amide.

questions.q: The diagram shows the skeletal formulas of four compounds, P, Q, R and S. Which two are successive members of the same homologous series?
optionWhy: Their molecular formulas, C₃H₆O and C₄H₈O, differ by CH₂, but P has an aldehyde group (C=O at the end of the chain) and Q a ketone group (C=O inside the chain). Members of one series share the same functional group.
Butanone (Q) and butanal (R) have the same molecular formula, C₄H₈O, with different functional groups: they are functional group isomers, not members of one series.

Butanal (R, C₄H₈O) and butan-1-ol (S, C₄H₁₀O) have the same number of carbon atoms and differ by H₂; they belong to different series (aldehydes and alcohols). Successive members differ by CH₂ and share a functional group.
P is propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO, and R is butanal, CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO: both have the aldehyde group –CHO and their formulas differ by one CH₂ unit, so they are successive aldehydes.
questions.explain: P is propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO, and R is butanal, CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO: both have the aldehyde group –CHO and their formulas differ by one CH₂ unit, so they are successive aldehydes.

questions.q: The boiling points of the first five straight-chain alkanes are: methane −162 °C, ethane −89 °C, propane −42 °C, butane −1 °C and pentane 36 °C. Which statement about this trend is correct?
options: Each further CH₂ unit adds the same rise as the last, 37 °C, so hexane is expected to boil at 73 °C.
The rise is caused by hydrogen bonding, which grows as H atoms are added to the chain.
The rise per CH₂ unit shrinks along the series, so hexane is expected to boil below 73 °C.
The rise occurs because longer molecules have more C–C and C–H bonds to break.
optionWhy: The steps in the data are 73, 47, 41 and 37 °C, not a constant: each extra CH₂ unit makes a smaller proportional difference to the London forces, so the next rise is less than 37 °C.
Alkanes have no O–H or N–H bonds and form no hydrogen bonds. The only forces between alkane molecules are London forces, which strengthen as the number of electrons increases.

The steps are 73, 47, 41 and 37 °C: each added CH₂ unit strengthens the London forces by a smaller fraction of an already larger molecule, so the next step is smaller than 37 °C and hexane boils below 73 °C (it boils at 69 °C).
Boiling separates molecules from one another; no covalent bonds are broken. The trend is due to stronger London forces between longer molecules with more electrons.
questions.explain: The steps are 73, 47, 41 and 37 °C: each added CH₂ unit strengthens the London forces by a smaller fraction of an already larger molecule, so the next step is smaller than 37 °C and hexane boils below 73 °C (it boils at 69 °C).
questions.working: Successive differences: −89 − (−162) = 73 °C; −42 − (−89) = 47 °C; −1 − (−42) = 41 °C; 36 − (−1) = 37 °C. The steps decrease, so the next step is smaller than 37 °C and hexane is expected to boil below 36 + 37 = 73 °C (it boils at 69 °C).

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂OH?
optionWhy: A student who gives the C=C bond the lowest number picks this. The group named as the suffix (-ol) has priority for the lowest locant; the double bond is numbered after it.
The chain has four carbon atoms. The –OH group, named by the suffix -ol, takes the lowest locant, 1. The C=C bond is then between carbons 3 and 4 and takes the lower number, 3: but-3-en-1-ol.
The –OH locant is right, but a C=C bond between carbons 3 and 4 takes the lower number, 3.
The suffix -al denotes an aldehyde (–CHO). This compound has a hydroxyl group, –OH, which takes the suffix -ol.
questions.explain: The chain has four carbon atoms. The –OH group, named by the suffix -ol, takes the lowest locant, 1. The C=C bond is then between carbons 3 and 4 and takes the lower number, 3: but-3-en-1-ol.

questions.q: The diagram shows the skeletal formula of a halogenoalkane. What is its IUPAC name?
optionWhy: Halogen and alkyl prefixes are listed together in alphabetical order, so bromo comes before methyl, whatever the locants: 2-bromo-3-methylhexane.

Carbon atoms sit at every end and vertex: the longest chain has six, so the parent is hexane. Numbering from the right-hand end gives the substituents the lowest locants, 2 and 3 (rather than 4 and 5 from the left). Prefixes are listed alphabetically: bromo before methyl.
The parent chain is the longest continuous chain, which runs through the propyl group: six carbon atoms. A four-carbon chain with a propyl branch is not the longest choice.

The chain is numbered from the end that gives the substituents the lowest locants, not from the left-hand end of the drawing. Numbering from the right gives 2 and 3, lower than 4 and 5, so the name is 2-bromo-3-methylhexane.
questions.explain: Carbon atoms sit at every end and vertex: the longest chain has six, so the parent is hexane. Numbering from the right-hand end gives the substituents the lowest locants, 2 and 3 (rather than 4 and 5 from the left). Prefixes are listed alphabetically: bromo before methyl.
questions.working: Longest continuous chain: six carbon atoms, so the parent is hexane. Numbering from the right-hand end puts Br on C2 and CH₃ on C3 (locants 2,3); from the left they would be 5,4. Prefixes in alphabetical order: bromo before methyl. Name: 2-bromo-3-methylhexane.

questions.q: The diagram shows the skeletal formula of a compound. What is its IUPAC name?
optionWhy: The functional group named by the suffix (-ol) takes priority for the lowest locant, so numbering starts from the OH end: 2-ol, 3-ene and 4-methyl.
A double bond is given the lower of the numbers of its two carbon atoms. Numbered from the OH end, the C=C joins carbons 3 and 4, so it is 3-ene; the methyl group is on carbon 4.

The hydroxyl group takes the suffix -ol and the lowest locant, so numbering starts at the right-hand end: OH on carbon 2, the C=C between carbons 3 and 4, named by its lower number, 3, and the methyl group on carbon 4.
The suffix -al denotes an aldehyde, –CHO. This compound has a hydroxyl group, –OH, on carbon 2, so the suffix is -ol: 4-methylpent-3-en-2-ol.
questions.explain: The hydroxyl group takes the suffix -ol and the lowest locant, so numbering starts at the right-hand end: OH on carbon 2, the C=C between carbons 3 and 4, named by its lower number, 3, and the methyl group on carbon 4.
questions.working: The suffix -ol takes the lowest locant, so number from the right-hand end: OH on C2, C=C between C3 and C4 (locant 3), methyl on C4. Name: 4-methylpent-3-en-2-ol.

questions.q: Which compound is a structural isomer of butan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH?
optionWhy: Ethoxyethane is C₄H₁₀O, the same molecular formula as butan-1-ol, but its atoms are connected differently (an alkoxy group instead of a hydroxyl group). It is a functional group isomer.
Butanal has four carbons and one oxygen, but its formula is C₄H₈O, two H atoms fewer than butan-1-ol (C₄H₁₀O). Isomers must have the same molecular formula.
This is butan-1-ol written from the other end. The atoms are connected in the same order, so it is the same compound, not an isomer.
Pentan-1-ol is C₅H₁₂O, one CH₂ more than butan-1-ol. It is the next member of the same homologous series, not an isomer.
questions.explain: Ethoxyethane is C₄H₁₀O, the same molecular formula as butan-1-ol, but its atoms are connected differently (an alkoxy group instead of a hydroxyl group). It is a functional group isomer.

questions.q: Which compound is a secondary halogenoalkane?
optionWhy: The Br is on carbon 2, but the class is not the locant. The carbon carrying Br is bonded to three other carbons (two CH₃ groups and a CH₂CH₃ group), so 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is tertiary.
In 3-bromopentane the carbon carrying the Br atom is bonded to two other carbon atoms (two CH₂ groups), so the compound is a secondary halogenoalkane.

Two Br atoms do not make a halogenoalkane secondary. The class depends on the carbon carrying the halogen, and here that carbon is bonded to only one other carbon atom, so the compound is not secondary.
The class counts carbon atoms, not hydrogen atoms, on the carbon carrying the halogen. That CH₂ carbon is bonded to one other carbon, so 1-bromopentane is primary.
questions.explain: In 3-bromopentane the carbon carrying the Br atom is bonded to two other carbon atoms (two CH₂ groups), so the compound is a secondary halogenoalkane.

questions.q: The diagram shows four skeletal formulas, P, Q, R and S. Which one represents a structural isomer of butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃?
optionWhy: P is butan-2-ol itself, drawn with the chain running the other way: OH on the third carbon from the left is OH on carbon 2 when numbered from the right. A different drawing is not a different compound.
S is 2-methylpropan-1-ol, CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂OH, molecular formula C₄H₁₀O, the same as butan-2-ol but with a branched chain: a structural isomer.
Q is but-3-en-2-ol, C₄H₈O. It has four carbon atoms and one oxygen, but two fewer hydrogen atoms than C₄H₁₀O, so its molecular formula differs and it is not an isomer.
R is pentan-2-ol, C₅H₁₂O, the next member of the same homologous series as butan-2-ol. Isomers must have the same molecular formula.
questions.explain: S is 2-methylpropan-1-ol, CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂OH, molecular formula C₄H₁₀O, the same as butan-2-ol but with a branched chain: a structural isomer.
